# Fixtures where the SELF-HOST wasm path disagrees with the native compiler.
#
# Format: <fixture-name> <#issue> <reason>
#
# TestFernFixturesSelfHostWasm lists these rather than skipping them, following
# tools/deadcode-allowlist.txt: the lane is green with them listed, a NEW
# divergence fails, and a listed fixture that starts PASSING also fails — an
# allowlist nobody prunes is where bugs go to be forgotten.
#
# `eq_struct_enum` and `ord_struct_enum` were here and are now FIXED (#6009):
# the self-host had no composite-comparison desugar at all, so `a == b` and
# `a < b` on a struct or enum lowered the two BOX POINTERS into a plain i32
# compare — structural equality answered "are these the same allocation" and
# ordering answered "which was allocated first". irlower now rewrites both to
# the type's derived `eq` / `cmp` the way the native checker does. The operator
# forms in self_host_derive_{eq,ord}_ir_test.go pin the shape directly.
#
# `audit_numeric_types` was here and is now FIXED (#6010): the self-host IR path
# applied its zero-cost-ascription rewrite (`var x: T = E as T` -> `var x: T = E`)
# to a real width conversion, so a narrowing `as u8` lost its mask in BINDING
# position only — 260 as u8 stayed 260 and the fixture's u8-wrap check returned 13.
# `cast_narrow_binding` now pins that shape directly.
#
# `tuple_match_expr` was here and is now FIXED (#6010): a tuple- or
# struct-pattern match in EXPRESSION position desugars into a done-flag if-chain
# whose arm bodies still ended in `return`, and a capturing IIFE lowers INLINE —
# so the arm returned from the ENCLOSING function and everything after the match
# was dead code. The arms now assign to a value local instead.
#
# `pure_collection_aliases` was here and is now FIXED (the #6007 slice): the
# self-host had no `Map.cleared` lowering at all — the name was known to the
# checker but nothing lowered it, so the module bailed on an unknown
# `Map.cleared` symbol. It is now construction: this runtime's map box is
# [keys, values] with no capacity field, so a fresh empty box of the same key
# kind IS a cleared map.
#
# `map_struct_value_field` was here and is now FIXED (the #6007 slice): its own
# header blames `get_or(..).field` on a Map[K, Struct], but that half always
# lowered — the bail was `it.value().field`, where expr_struct_type had a struct
# recovery for the get_or receiver and none for the iterator's. Both read the
# same V.
#
# `derive_json` was here and is now FIXED, in two halves. (1) Every @derive over
# an enum VARIANT bound a single `__p0`, so `Rect(2, 3)` serialised, compared,
# ordered and hashed as `Rect(2)` — derived `eq` answered TRUE for
# `Rect(2, 3) == Rect(2, 9)`; pinned by `derive_multi_payload`. (2) With that
# gone, `.to_json()` on an `i32[]` FIELD receiver was seen to render the array
# POINTER: the guard listing the array predicates relies on expr_is_arr_src for
# scalar arrays, and that means array SOURCE (fresh/owned, an rc concept), not
# "is an array", so a field READ fell through to the primitive path. Pinned by
# `json_array_field`.
#
# The four `regex_*` capture rows were here and are now FIXED (#6008). Their
# header called them "plausibly one root cause" in "how std/regex's capture
# handling lowers"; that guess was half right. It WAS one cause, but nothing
# in it was about captures — the trigger was `var p = xs.append(v)` on a
# BORROWED array PARAM.
#
# `__fern_arr_push` grows the receiver IN PLACE and hands the SAME pointer back
# when the buffer is uniquely referenced with spare capacity. On a borrowed
# param that buffer belongs to the CALLER, so the binding aliased it while
# irlower marked the slot a fresh rc=1 move — and both frames released it on
# supersede. `__rx_emit` recurses, so one `RInst[]` was aliased across three
# frames; the third release pushed a LIVE block onto the freelist, and
# `__rx_fill`'s `seen` array was handed that block on top of an `ISplit`'s
# `RSplit` payload. The Pike VM then read a garbage jump target and branched to
# `prog[-1]`, which is the `unreachable` these four hit. A capturing group was
# required only because `ISave`'s `caps.with(slot, ti)` is the sole allocator in
# the epsilon closure — i.e. the only thing that RECYCLED the freed block. That
# is why `(?:b)?` and `b?` looked fine: same double free, nothing to make it
# visible.
#
# irlower now rewrites that BIND to `p = xs[0 : xs.len()].append(v)` so the
# bound slot is the fresh rc=1 array it was already marked as. Only the bind
# changed: `return xs.append(v)` still grows in place, because there the caller
# reassigns the slot it lent out. That distinction is load-bearing, not
# tidiness — routing return position to the clone form as well took a 20k-append
# accumulator chain from 3 ms to 11.7 s, which is the #4873 fast path.
#
# The x86-64 leg had reported these same fixtures CLEAN, which is why the bug
# read as wasm-specific for so long. It was not: the double free happens on
# every backend, and `__rc_underflow_count()` shows it there too. x86-64 simply
# does not recycle the freed block onto anything that matters. The fixture
# `rc_borrowed_param_append` pins the refcount directly rather than the symptom,
# so it fails on x86-64 and arm64 as well.
#
# One of the original twelve remains. All were found by the leg's first run
# over the existing corpus, on fixtures that had been green for months because
# all four of TestFernFixtures' backends are the native compiler. Each has been reproduced by hand with a
# native self-host CLI (`make selfhost-cli`) before being written down; none is
# a harness artifact. The first pass reported 26 mismatches and 14 of those WERE
# artifacts — WASI caps exit status at 125, so nine regex fixtures whose expected
# 255 is a feature bitmask looked like a broken regex engine — which is why every
# entry here names a measured before/after rather than a symptom.

# --- the self-host wasm path cannot lower these at all --------------------
# Hard errors now the AST emitters are deleted (#3457), so these are real
# IR-subset gaps, not fallbacks. "module is not IR-eligible" from the driver.
generic_method_typeparams #6007 IR-ineligible on self-host wasm; native compiles it

# --- traps at runtime ----------------------------------------------------
# None. The four #6008 rows that lived here are fixed; see the note above.

# --- the exit>=126 blind spot, and how to see through it -----------------
# WASI refuses any status outside [0..126), so a fixture whose expected exit is
# >= 126 reports 1 here no matter what it computed. `regex_captures_assert`
# (expected 255) and `regex_groups` (expected 127) sat in this file's tail as
# "suspicious but unmeasurable", with a note asking for a stdout-based oracle.
# One was not needed: the SELF-HOST X86-64 leg runs the same irlower over the
# same corpus and carries main's return over the full 0..255. Reading a
# suspicious wasm fixture there costs nothing and answers the question outright.
#
# Doing that settled both. `regex_captures_assert` really was broken — it
# returned 47 for 255 — and it was the same #6008 double free, not a separate
# defect; it now returns 255 on x86-64 and stops short of the ceiling on wasm.
# `regex_groups` measured 127 on x86-64 both before and after the fix, so its
# recorded "111" was never a divergence in the first place. Neither is listed.
#
# So: when this leg cannot see a value, ask the x86-64 leg before writing down a
# symptom. Six regex fixtures were carried here on measurements the sibling leg
# could have priced exactly.
